ideas.title: Why Stores Doubled Shopping Cart Sizes
ideas.angle: Reveals how doubling the physical volume of shopping carts tricks the human brain into buying 40% more items without realizing it, exposing grocery retail architecture. Comment trigger asks viewers whether they grab a basket or cart and what their biggest accidental grocery bill was.

hook.en: Stop grabbing that giant shopping cart.

ideas.reason: Retail dark patterns and grocery store psychology consistently pull tens of millions of views on short-form platforms because every single viewer buys groceries and relates to spending more than planned.
sources: Martin Lindstrom, 'Brandwashed: Tricks Companies Use to Manipulate Our Minds and Persuade Us to Buy'
Journal of Marketing Research retail floor and container studies

ideas.title: Why Fancy Menus Remove Dollar Signs
ideas.angle: Exposes why luxury restaurants remove dollar symbols ($) and write raw digits like '24' instead of '$24.00' to erase the psychological 'pain of paying'. Built-in test challenges viewers to check the last menu they saw and comment whether they fell for it.

hook.en: Notice the dollar signs are missing?

ideas.reason: Cornell University's famous menu study is an undeniable, highly verifiable fact that gives viewers an instant 'aha!' realization next time they sit at any dining establishment.
sources: Cornell University School of Hotel Administration study on menu price presentation
MIT & Carnegie Mellon studies on neural 'pain of paying'

ideas.title: The Refund Trick That Keeps Your Money
ideas.angle: Unpacks the 'Endowment Effect' weaponized by digital subscription brands: offering a 50% discount or 30-day free extension right when you hit cancel, making your brain feel like you are losing free cash. Comment prompt asks viewers what app subscription they are currently trapped in.

hook.en: They want you to hit cancel.

ideas.reason: Directly targets subscription fatigue, a massive viral trend in 2024-2025 as consumers fight rising digital subscription costs and predatory churn reduction flows.
sources: Federal Trade Commission (FTC) Dark Patterns in Subscription Renewals Report
Daniel Kahneman and Richard Thaler behavioral economics research on loss aversion
